The measured in-band functional leader is now [7,7,5,3] at 0.796032 Å / 3.625916 pIC50, ahead of [7,7,3,3] 0.796170 / 3.625929, [7,9,7,5] 0.795404 / 3.626143, and [7,9,7,7] 0.795003 / 3.626289. Interval-1 7->9 is measured adverse on the [7,7,7,7] background ([7,9,7,7] 3.626289 vs [7,7,7,7] 3.626162, +1.27e-4 pIC50), so high-side interval-1 probes are ranked below supported release tests. data.failure_directions: G2:H1 fails if interval-3 release below 3 saturates at 3, giving gap >=3.625916 pIC50 or condition >0.7970 Å; then keep interval 3 at 3 and retain [7,7,5,3]. G3:H1 fails if release below 3 is null or adverse on [7,7,3,_], giving gap >=3.625929 pIC50 or condition >0.7970 Å. G1:H1 fails if gap >=3.625916 pIC50 or condition >0.7970 Å, or if its interval-2 release is non-additive and the arm is worse than G1:H2. G1:H2 fails if interval-3 release 5->3 on [7,9,7,5] does not improve the gap by at least ~5e-5 pIC50, which would leave interval-3 function minimum at 5 and undercut G1:H1's interval-3 component. G2:H2 and G3:H2 are high-side interval-1=9 probes after a measured adverse edge; they are not forecast to beat the leader and are ranked low. No Best-driven selection is justified.
